sources.title: Entry regime of Ukraine for foreign citizens
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: Ukraine MFA's official entry-regime table directly maps the named EU passports to visa-free entry, but identifies itself as of 8 June 2023 and is supporting context rather than fresh controlling proof.

policies.title: Named EU ordinary passports: Ukraine short-visit visa waiver
policies.summary: Ukraine's live current-edition Presidential Decree waives visas for citizens of EU Member States entering or transiting Ukraine for stays not exceeding 90 days.
conditions: Applies to a citizen of the named current EU Member State travelling on that state's standard ordinary passport for a short visitor entry or transit.
The Ukrainian Decree itself establishes the named EU-Member-State class; this is not an inference from EU or Schengen rules applicable elsewhere.

The Rada portal prints the operative decree as the current edition without a lost-force marker, but does not explicitly label its legal status as in force. The Ukraine MFA's June 2023 table directly corroborates the named visa-free outcomes; this metadata/currentness limitation keeps the cohort at medium confidence.
The Decree states a stay may not exceed 90 days. It does not itself state an 180-day calculation, so none is asserted here.
Work, residence, diplomatic, service, emergency and other special travel documents, wartime operational access, and final admission remain outside this baseline.

conflicts.officialStatus: unresolved: current Luxembourg guidance requires a pre-travel e-Tourist Visa
conflicts.explanation: Luxembourg's current traveller guidance directly rejects visa-free travel, while the linked Ukrainian eVisa service cannot be replayed and Ukraine's own direct visa-free table is dated June 2023. No single current replacement route is safely established.

unresolved.reason: Luxembourg's January 2026 guidance directly requires a pre-travel e-Tourist Visa, contradicting the indeterminate-force decree record and Ukraine's June 2023 visa-free table. The linked Ukrainian application service cannot be replayed, so eVisa is not promoted as a replacement.
